movement_source: row 'Loan impairment expense', column FY25 -> column FY26
headline: CBA's loan impairment expense increased $62 million (9%) to $788 million in FY26 from $726 million in FY25. The annualised loss rate rose to 8 bps of average gross loans and acceptances (GLAA) from 7 bps. The increase was driven by higher collective provisions ($150m), partially offset by a reduction in individually assessed net charges ($17m). Divisionally, Retail Banking Services drove the rise (+$106m), while Business Banking (-$45m) and Institutional Banking (-$16m) provided offsets.

drivers.narrative: Collective provisions increased $150 million to $606 million (ev-3, ev-4). Corporate collective provisions rose $172 million to $2,797 million due to portfolio growth and macroeconomic uncertainty (ev-14). Consumer collective provisions fell $48 million to $2,888 million as rising house prices offset cost-of-living pressures (ev-15).

drivers.bank_label: Net new and increased individual provisioning
drivers.narrative: Net new/increased individual provisions decreased $17 million to $422 million (ev-3, ev-5). Corporate individually assessed provisions fell $6 million to $694 million (ev-17). Consumer individually assessed provisions fell $19 million to $97 million (ev-16).

limitations: The bank does not explicitly split collective provisions into 'volume' vs 'asset quality' drivers in the quantified bridge; the narrative attributes movements to both factors.
